data.name: Andersen
data.gender_notes: Andersen is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Andersen is derived from the Old Norse 'Ander' meaning man and 'sen' meaning strong, warrior. In Christian context, Andersen may be associated with St. Andrew, the patron saint of Scotland, fishermen, and single people. The name Andersen carries the meaning “Man, warrior” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Andersen usually hope their child will grow to embody man, warrior and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Carrying the spirit of a strong warrior, Andersen embodies courage, faith, and determination.
data.etymology: Andersen belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Man, warrior.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Andersen total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.
data.cultural_impact: Andersen is a distinctively Scandinavian name with roots deeply connected to Norse mythology. It's associated with Scandinavian heritage, a strong sense of history, and a proud connection to the Viking past.
data.spiritual_significance: In Christianity, the name Andersen may symbolize strength and courage given by God to overcome trials and challenges. It may also evoke the spiritual presence and intercession of St. Andrew, the patron saint associated with this name. For singles, Andersen may serve as a reminder of faith and trust, believing that the right partner and happy union will come in time. For all Christians named Andersen, the name calls for a strong faith, resilience, and courage in life's journey.

historical_references.reference: The name Andersen has been used throughout Christian history by saints, scholars, and faithful believers who exemplified its meaning.

modern_usage.modern_context: Andersen is a common Danish surname, originating from the Old Norse personal name Ander, meaning 'man' or 'warrior'. It is one of the most common surnames in Denmark, and is also found in other Scandinavian countries.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted Christian named Hannah Andersen in New York, United States credits much of their spiritual journey to their name Andersen, which means "Man, warrior". They believe their name has been a blessing and reminder of God's presence in their life.
